nahhas-irab:89-89.t: قالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما: Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the proof that the supplication belonged to both of them together is the saying of Moses ﷺ «ربّنا» ("our Lord"), and he did not say «ربّ» ("my Lord"). فَاسْتَقِيما: al-Farrāʾ said: they were both commanded to remain upright in their affair and to stand firm in it until the fulfilment of the answer came to them. He said: and it is said that between the two there were forty years. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: between the two there were forty years. وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) as a prohibition; the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd); it was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and kasra was chosen for it because it resembles the nūn of the dual.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: قالَ آمَنْتُ أَنَّهُ: it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), the meaning being «بأنه» ("in that He…"). Whoever reads «إنّه» with kasra, the implied meaning for him is: he said, "I have become a believer," and then «إنه» begins anew; and Abū Ḥātim claimed that the verb of saying is omitted. وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). We have already mentioned the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ from Gabriel ﷺ that he put mud into his mouth, and the interpretation of this — and Allah knows best — is that it was a punishment for the enemy of Allah.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: so he was brought out for them. They said: "so that you may be a sign for those after you," so that they would know that he was not a god. As al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: نُنَجِّيكَ is from al-najāʾ and al-injāʾ (rescue); and some of them said: "We raise you onto a raised place (najwa) of the land." He said: بِبَدَنِكَ means "with no soul in you." He said: and the saying of whoever said that «ببدنك» means "with your coat of mail" is worth nothing.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ. We have already mentioned its meaning.

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: وَلَوْ جاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ: «كلّ» was given feminine agreement according to the meaning, because the meaning is "even if the signs came to them."

nahhas-irab:98-98.t:
فَلَوْلا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ: al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī said: it means «فهلّا» ("why then not…"). Al-Farrāʾ said: and in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «فهلا», because its meaning is that they did not believe. Someone else said: the meaning is "no town believed among those against whom the words of your Lord came true," i.e. the people of a town. إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ is accusative because it is an exception that is not from the first [category] (disjoined exception), i.e. "but the people of Yūnus." This is the view of al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ, and Sībawayh recited:
[al-Kāmil] 203-
من كان أسرع في تفرّق فالج ... فلبونه جربت معا وأغدّت
إلّا كناشرة الّذي ضيّعتم ... كالغصن في غلوائه المتنبّت
(Whoever was quicker to break up [the tribe of] Fālij, may his milch-camels all catch mange and plague — except [one] like Nāshira, whom you neglected, like a branch sprouting in its full growth.)
And إلّا قومُ يونس with the nominative is permissible, and Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz] 204-
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلّا اليعافير وإلّا العيس
(And many a land in which there is no companion except the gazelles and except the white camels.)
Its nominative, according to Sībawayh, is from two angles: one of them is that the first is [treated as] emphasis [Translator's note: the text reads «توكيدا» as written]; the other angle is that he makes the gazelles and the white camels its companions. Among the best things said about the nominative is what Abū Isḥāq said; he said: the meaning would be "other than (ghayr) the people of Yūnus," and when he brought «إلّا» he declined the noun after it with the declension of «غير», as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 205-
وكلّ أخ مفارقه أخوه ... لعمر أبيك إلّا الفرقدان
(Every brother will be parted from by his brother — by the life of your father — except the two Farqad stars.)

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ: tawkīd (emphasis) of «مَن». جَمِيعاً is, according to Sībawayh, accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: وَيَجْعَلُ الرِّجْسَ, i.e. the punishment, عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ, i.e. who do not understand the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they are the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: وَما تُغْنِي is in the position of the nominative; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, and the yāʾ was dropped from pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Likewise نُنَجِّيكَ is in the position of the nominative. «وما» is in the position of the accusative by «يعني» [Translator's note: so in the text; «تغني» is presumably meant], and it is a complete noun.

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: فَلا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ: [«أعبد»] is nominative by virtue of being imperfect (muḍāraʿa); likewise أَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحاكِمِينَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), because He, Majestic and Mighty, judges only with the truth. It is reported from Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim: إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ [Yūnus: 98] with kasra on the nūn, and likewise «يوسف» with kasra on the sīn. Abū Ḥātim said: if they use kasra, they must use a hamza, because they imagine it to be from ānasa yuʾnisu and āsafa yuʾsifu. He said: and Abū Zayd said: some Arabs say يونِس and يوسِف.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb read to me [Translator's note: the source has «قرأ عليّ أحمد بن شعيب بن علي بن الحسين بن حريث», which merges two links of the chain; elsewhere the chain runs Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ← ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth]: he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn informed us, from his father, from Yazīd, that ʿIkrima narrated to him from Ibn ʿAbbās: «الر» and «حم» and «ن» are "al-Raḥmān" separated. [Yazīd said:] I narrated it to al-Aʿmash, and he said: "You have things like this and you do not tell me?" Abū Jaʿfar said: We mentioned in Sūrat al-Baqara that Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah's mercy be upon him, said: the meaning of «الر» is "I am Allah; I see" (anā llāhu arā). I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining towards this view, because Sībawayh reported the like of it from the Arabs, and recited: [al-Rajaz] 195-
بالخير خيرات وإن شرّا فا ... ولا أريد الشّرّ إلّا أن تا
("With good, good things; and if evil, then [evil]; and I do not want evil unless you [will].")
Sībawayh said: He means "if evil, then evil; and I do not want evil unless you will (tashāʾ)". Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima said: «الر» is an oath. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: «الر» is the name of the sūra; he said: and so is every spelled-out letter group in the Qur'an. Mujāhid said: They are the openings of the sūras. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: It is a call to attention, and so are the letters of the alphabet [at the openings]. (تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. those that have been mentioned are the verses of the wise Book; if you wish, the implied form is "these — those are the verses of the wise Book". Abū ʿUbayda said: «الحكيم» means "made firm" (al-muḥkam).
(أَكانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا إِلى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ قالَ الْكافِرُونَ إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ) (2). (أَكانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً): the khabar of kāna, and its ism is (أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «أكان للناس عجب», as the ism of kāna, the khabar being (أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا). (أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن أنذر الناس» ("that you warn mankind"), and likewise (أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ). «إنّ لهم قدم صدق» [with kasra] is also permissible, meaning "say: …".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (دَعْواهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. their supplication. (فِيها سُبْحانَكَ): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and likewise (وَآخِرُ دَعْواهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ). Abū ʿUbayd reported only the lightened «أن» with the nominative after it. He said: We think they chose this and distinguished it from His words, Majestic and Mighty, (أَنَّ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ) and (أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ) [al-Nūr: 7, 9] [Translator's note: the source gives only «[النور: 9]»], because they intended to quote what is said: «الحمد لله». Abū Jaʿfar said: The position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that this «أن» is lightened from the heavy one, and the meaning is «أنه الحمد لله» ("that [the fact is]: praise be to Allah"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «أن الحمد لله» [with the accusative, al-ḥamda] is also permissible, making it govern when light as it governs when heavy; but the nominative is more in line with analogy, because it resembles the verb only in form, not in meaning, so when it falls short of the verb it does not govern as the verb does; whoever uses the accusative likens it to the verb when something is dropped from it. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Ḥātim reported that Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read (وَآخِرُ دَعْواهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) [Translator's note: i.e. anna l-ḥamda, with the heavy anna and the accusative; the source prints the standard vowelling].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
(وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجالَهُمْ بِالْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ): it is said that its meaning is: if Allah hastened punishment for people as they seek to hasten reward and good, and punished them, they would die, because they were created in this world with a weak constitution; and they will not be so on the Day of Resurrection, because on the Day of Resurrection they will be created for permanence. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned a view other than this. «استعجالهم», according to the view of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ, means «كاستعجالهم» ("like their seeking to hasten"); then the kāf was dropped and it was put in the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: As you say «ضربت زيدا ضربك», i.e. "like your striking". As for the position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — and it is the right one — the implied form in it is "if Allah hastened evil for people with a hastening like their seeking to hasten good"; then «تعجيلا» was omitted and its qualifier was put in its place, then its qualifier was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place, like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ). Sībawayh reported «زيد شرب الإبل» ("Zayd drinks the drinking of camels"). If what al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said were permissible, «زيد الأسد» would be permissible in the sense of "like the lion"; this is very clear.
Abū Isḥāq said: It is also read (لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. la-qaḍā ilayhim ajalahum, active; the source prints the standard vowelling], which is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī; it is a good reading because it is connected with His words, Majestic and Mighty, (وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ). Al-Akhfash said: (فَنَذَرُ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا) is a new beginning. He said: (يَعْمَهُونَ) means they wander in confusion.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
(وَإِذا مَسَّ الْإِنْسانَ الضُّرُّ دَعانا لِجَنْبِهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَوْ قاعِداً): conjoined to the position; the implied form is "he calls on Us lying down, or sitting, or standing". (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنا): al-Akhfash said: It is the heavy «أنّ», lightened, as [the poet] said: [al-Khafīf] 197-
وي كأن من يكن له نشب يحبب ... ومن يفتقر يعش عيش ضرّ
("Ah! It seems that whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.")

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (ثُمَّ جَعَلْناكُمْ خَلائِفَ): two objects. (لِنَنْظُرَ): accusative by the lām of kay (purpose).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا): the noun of a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. Abū Isḥāq said: (بَيِّناتٍ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: (قُلْ لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا أَدْراكُمْ بِهِ): i.e. had Allah willed, He would not have sent me to you so that I recited the Qur'an to you, nor would He have made you know it, i.e. the Qur'an. Abū Ḥātim said: I heard al-Aṣmaʿī say: I asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ about al-Ḥasan's reading «ولا أدرأتكم به» — does it have a valid construction? He said: No. Abū ʿUbayd said: Al-Ḥasan's reading «ولا أدرأتكم به» has no valid construction except as a mistake. The meaning of Abū ʿUbayd's saying "as a mistake", if Allah wills, is that one says darītu, i.e. I knew, and adraytu someone else [I made him know]; and one says daraʾtu, i.e. I repelled; so a confusion occurs between darītu, adraytu and daraʾtu. Abū Ḥātim said: Al-Ḥasan means — so I reckon — «ولا أدريتكم به», and he replaced the yāʾ with an alif according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb, because they replace yāʾ with alif when what precedes it has fatḥa, as in (إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ) [Ṭāhā: 63]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake, because the transmission from al-Ḥasan is «ولا أدرأتكم به» with hamza, while Abū Ḥātim spoke of it as being without hamza. It may be from daraʾtu, when I repelled, i.e. "nor would I have commanded you to repel and abandon disbelief in the Qur'an". (فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُراً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ): there is an omission in the sentence; the implied form is "I have stayed among you a lifetime before it, while you knew me for truthfulness and trustworthiness, not reading or writing; then I came to you with the miracles". (أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ) that this could only be from Allah, Majestic and Mighty?

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (وَما كانَ النَّاسُ إِلَّا أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): the ism of «كان» and its khabar (predicate). (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): in the position of the naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: (فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ): the original is «أنني» [i.e. innanī]; the nūn was dropped. The meaning is: "a waiter among those who wait".

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: (وَإِذا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً): the answer of «إذا», according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is (إِذا لَهُمْ مَكْرٌ فِي آياتِنا), the implied sense being "they plotted". Mujāhid said: «إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا» means mockery and denial. (قُلِ اللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (مَكْراً): by way of clarification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «يسيّركم» carries the sense of intensity/frequency, while «يسيركم» [yusīrukum] is for little and much. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «هو الذي ينشركم» ("it is He who spreads you"), and it is the known reading of al-Ḥasan. «يسيّركم» fits better with His words, Majestic and Mighty, (وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ). (والْفُلْكِ) is masculine and feminine, and it is singular and also the plural of «فلك», as one says «وثن» and «وثن» [wathan and wuthn]. (جاءَتْها): the hāʾ refers back to the ships, and it may also refer back to the good wind. (رِيحٌ عاصِفٌ).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (إِنَّما بَغْيُكُمْ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) [Translator's note: i.e. matāʿu in the nominative; the source prints the accusative vowelling of Ḥafṣ]. Its khabar may also be (عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ), and you imply a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that is the enjoyment of the life of this world" or "it is the enjoyment of the life of this world". There is a subtle difference between the two meanings. If you put «متاع» in the nominative as the khabar of «بغيكم», the meaning is "the transgression of some of you against others is only …", like (فَسَلِّمُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ) [al-Nūr: 61], and likewise (لَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ) [al-Tawba: 128]. If the khabar is «على أنفسكم», the meaning is "your corruption only comes back upon you", like (وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها) [al-Isrāʾ: 7]. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read (مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (إِنَّما مَثَلُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (كَماءٍ): its khabar (predicate), and the kāf is in the position of the nominative. (أَنْزَلْناهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ): a naʿt (adjective) for «ماء». (فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَباتُ الْأَرْضِ): conjoined. (حَتَّى إِذا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَها وَازَّيَّنَتْ): the original is «تزيّنت»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought, because the assimilated letter stands for two letters, the first of which is quiescent. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Abū al-ʿĀliya read (وَازَّيَّنَتْ) [Translator's note: i.e. wa-azyanat; the source prints the standard vowelling], i.e. it brought forth adornment; the verb is given in its original form — had it been made weak, it would be «أزانت». ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī said: Our elders read «وازيانّت», whose pattern is like «واسوادّت». In the transmission of al-Muqaddamī: «وازّاينت», whose original is «تزاينت», on the pattern tafāʿalat, then assimilated. (وَظَنَّ أَهْلُها أَنَّهُمْ قادِرُونَ عَلَيْها): Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "able to benefit from it". (أَتاها أَمْرُنا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهاراً): two adverbials (ẓarf). (فَجَعَلْناها حَصِيداً): two objects.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَزِيادَةٌ): conjoined to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ that the "increase" is looking upon Allah the Exalted. It is also said: the increase is that a good deed is multiplied tenfold and more than that. Al-Ḥasan read (وَلا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلا ذِلَّةٌ) [Translator's note: i.e. qatrun, with sukūn; the source prints the standard vowelling]. «القتر», «القتر» and «القترة» [qatar, qatr and qatara] have one meaning.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (قِطَعاً): plural of «قطعة». (مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الليل»; it is unlikely to be a naʿt (adjective) for «قطع», because He did not say «مظلمة». Al-Kisāʾī read (قِطَعاً) with sukūn on the ṭāʾ [qiṭʿan]; on this reading «مظلما» is a naʿt, and it may also be a ḥāl from «الليل».

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: Some read (فزايلنا بينهم) [Translator's note: i.e. fa-zāyalnā, instead of fa-zayyalnā]. One says «لا أزايل فلانا», i.e. "I do not part from so-and-so"; but if you say «لا أزاوله», it has another meaning: "I do not try to deceive him".

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (شَهِيداً): accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Abū Isḥāq said: It may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (ما مِنْ شَفِيعٍ): in the position of the nominative; the meaning is "there is no intercessor (إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ)".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
(هُنالِكَ): in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. at that time. (تَبْلُوا كُلُّ نَفْسٍ). The lām [in «هنالك»] is additional, given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the kāf is for address and has no grammatical position. Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 198-
هنالك إن يستخبلوا المال يخبلوا ... وإن يسألوا يعطوا وإن ييسروا يغلوا
("There, if they are asked to lend property, they lend it; if they are asked, they give; and if they play at the gaming-arrows, they choose the costly [camels].")
(وَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الْحَقِّ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective), and likewise «الحقّ». «الحق» may be in the accusative in three ways: the implied form may be "they were returned truly", and then the alif and lām were brought; the implied form may be "their master truly, not what they worship besides Him"; and the third way is that it be praise, i.e. "I mean the True". It is also permissible to put «الحقّ» in the nominative, the meaning being "their master is the True, not what they associate besides Him". (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): in the position of the nominative, and it has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. their fabrication.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (فَذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ): the accusative of «الحق» is also permissible, as explained above.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (كَذلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا أَنَّهُمْ): the meaning is «بأنّهم» and «لأنهم» ("in that they" / "because they"), so «أنّ» is in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: It may also be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «كلمات» [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading being discussed here is «كلمة»]. Al-Farrāʾ said: (أَنَّهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) is permissible with kasra of «إنّ», as a new sentence.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
(أَمَّنْ): al-Akhfash said: If someone asks, "How can «أم» come in upon «من»?", it is said: because «أم» and the alif are the basis of interrogation; do you not see that «أم» indicates «هل»?
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are five readings of (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي). Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read «أم من لا يهدّي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahaddī]; and so Warsh related from Nāfiʿ. Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa narrated to me: he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to me: he said: Qālūn narrated to me from Nāfiʿ that he read «أم من لا يهدّي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahddī]. Abū ʿUbayd said: ʿĀṣim read (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي) with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yahiddī]. Al-Kisāʾī said: ʿĀṣim read «أم من لا يهدي» with kasra on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and doubling of the dāl [yihiddī]. These are four readings. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «أم من لا يهدي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the hāʾ and a light dāl [yahdī].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is clear in Arabic: its original is «يهتدي»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and its vowel was transferred to the hāʾ. The third reading is the one known from ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ: the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ is meant] was assimilated into the dāl, and the hāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The second reading, which Qālūn related from Nāfiʿ, represents a combination of two quiescent letters; this is not permissible, and no one is able to pronounce it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Whoever attempts the like of this must make a slight movement towards kasra; Sībawayh calls this "snatching the vowel" (ikhtilās al-ḥaraka). As for the kasra of the yāʾ together with the hāʾ, which al-Kisāʾī related from ʿĀṣim, it is not permissible according to Sībawayh. Sībawayh permits «تهدي», «نهدي» and «إهدي» [tihiddī, nihiddī, ihiddī — Translator's note: the source prints «تهدي ويهدي وأهدي»] and does not permit «يهدي» [yihiddī], because kasra on the yāʾ is heavy. As for the fifth reading, «أم من لا يهدي», it has two constructions in Arabic, though it is far-fetched. One of the two is that al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: «يهدي» means «يهتدي» ("is guided"). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: This is not known; rather, the implied form is "or one who does not guide another" — the sentence is complete; then He said (إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدى), an exception not of the same kind as the first, i.e. "but he himself needs to be guided", as you say «فلان لا يشبع غيره إلّا أن يشبع» ("so-and-so does not satisfy anyone else's hunger, except that he be fed"), i.e. but he himself needs to be fed. Abū Isḥāq said: (فَما لَكُمْ) — the sentence is complete, and the meaning is "what do you have in worshipping idols?" (كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ): he said: (كَيْفَ) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "in what state?".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
(وَما كانَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرى مِنْ دُونِ): al-Kisāʾī said: The meaning is "this Qur'an is not a fabrication", as you say «فلان يحبّ أن يركب» and «يحبّ الركوب» ("he likes to ride" / "he likes riding"). Someone else said: The implied form is «لأن يفترى» ("to be fabricated"). Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is "it is not fitting for this Qur'an to be fabricated". Someone else said: The meaning is "no one could produce the like of this Qur'an from other than Allah and then attribute it to Allah", because of its inimitability in its arrangement, its meanings and its composition.
(وَلكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Muḥammad ibn Saʿdān said: The implied form is "but it was a confirmation of what was before it". According to them the nominative is also permissible, meaning "but it is a confirmation"; and likewise (وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): «أم» in the sense of «بل» ("rather"), and it carries the sense of making them acknowledge (taqrīr), so as to establish the argument against them.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِما لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ): i.e. they denied it while ignorant of its meanings and interpretation, whereas they were obliged to learn that by asking. (وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ): i.e. they denied it without knowing its interpretation; it is also said: and there has not yet come to them what its matter will lead to. (كَذلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): i.e. such was their way; the kāf is in the position of the accusative. (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الظَّالِمِينَ): «كيف» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (جَمِيعاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "your return" is "He has promised you". (حَقًّا): a maṣdar, accusative. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «وعد الله» in the nominative, meaning "your return to Him is the promise of Allah". Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: he makes it the khabar (predicate) of «مرجعكم». Al-Farrāʾ also permitted «وعد الله حقّ». Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read (إِنَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ) [Translator's note: i.e. annahu, with fatḥa; the source prints the standard vowelling], with «أنّ» in the position of the accusative, i.e. "He promised you that He originates creation"; the implied form may also be "because He originates creation", as one says «لبّيك أن الحمد والنّعمة لك» ("at Your service — for praise and grace are Yours"). The kasra is better. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «أنّ» to be in the position of the nominative. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: the implied form is then "truly, the originating of creation".

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ): i.e. in the future; «من» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ). The meaning is: and among them is one who persists in his disbelief. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He delayed the punishment from them only because among them are some who will believe. (وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ): i.e. of those who persist in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (وَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ لِي عَمَلِي): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is "mine is the recompense of my deeds"; and likewise (وَلَكُمْ عَمَلُكُمْ). (أَنْتُمْ بَرِيئُونَ مِمَّا أَعْمَلُ وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): the same.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ): [the plural is] according to the meaning [of «من»].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ): [the singular is] according to the wording [of «من»].

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
(وَلكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): a group of grammarians, among them al-Farrāʾ, claimed that when the Arabs say «ولكنّ» with the wāw they prefer the doubled form, and when they drop the wāw they prefer the light form. Al-Farrāʾ gave a reason for this; he said: Because without the wāw it resembles «بل», so they lightened it so that what follows it would be like what follows «بل»; and when they brought the wāw it differed from «بل», so they doubled it and put [the following noun] in the accusative by it, because it is «إنّ» with a lām and a kāf added to it, made into a single particle. He recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 199-
ولكنّني من حبّها لكميد
("But I, from love of her, am surely grief-stricken.")
He brought the lām because it is «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
(كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا): in the sense of «كأنّهم لم يلبثوا» ("as if they had not tarried"). (يَتَعارَفُونَ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ): this may be a statement from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, after He has pointed to the resurrection and the raising; and the meaning may be that they recognise one another, saying this among themselves.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً): two objects. (وَالْقَمَرَ نُوراً): conjoined. (وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنازِلَ): in the sense of "and He determined for it", like (وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ) [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3]; it is also possible that the meaning is "He made it possessed of stations", like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. He said «وقدّره» and did not say «وقدّرهما», though the sun and the moon both have stations; there are two answers to this. One is that He singled out the moon because ordinary people know the months by it. The other answer is that [the pronoun] is omitted from the first because the second indicates it; Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 196-
رماني بأمر كنت منه ووالدي ... بريئا ومن جول الطّويّ رماني
("He accused me of a thing of which I and my father were innocent; and from the side of the well he cast it at me.")
(لِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسابَ): on the basis that it is the nūn of the [sound masculine] plural. Some Arabs say «عدد السّنين والحساب» [Translator's note: presumably al-sinīni, declining on the nūn; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. Some Arabs say «سنوات» and some say «سنهات», and the diminutive is «سنيهة» and «سنيّة». It is permissible to pluralise them with wāw and nūn as compensation for what was dropped from them, and the first letter is given kasra as an indication of what has been attached to it that properly belongs to others. (ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, intended nothing by creating that except wisdom and rightness.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا): the ism of inna, and the khabar (predicate) is (أُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ).
